entries.title: Acts 24:1
segments: Five days afterwards the High Priest Ananias came down with some of the Councillors and a barrister named Tertullus. They laid an information with the Governor against Paul;

entries.title: Acts 24:2
segments: And, when the hearing came on, Tertullus began his speech for the prosecution.

entries.title: Acts 24:3
segments: "We owe it to your Excellency," he said, "that we are enjoying profound peace, and we owe it to your foresight that this nation is constantly securing reforms--advantages which we very gratefully accept at all times and places.

entries.title: Acts 24:4
segments: But--not to be tedious--I beg you, with your accustomed fairness, to listen to a brief statement of our case.

entries.title: Acts 24:5
segments: We have found this man a public pest; he is one who stirs up disputes among the Jews all the world over, and is a ringleader of the Nazarene heretics.

entries.title: Acts 24:6
segments: He even attempted to desecrate the Temple itself, but we caught him;

entries.title: Acts 24:7
segments: (Translation omits this verse)

entries.title: Acts 24:8
segments: And you will be able, by examining him on all these points, to satisfy yourself as to the charges which we are bringing against him."

entries.title: Acts 24:9
segments: The Jews also joined in the attack and bore out his statements.

entries.title: Acts 24:10
segments: On a sign from the Governor, Paul made this reply: "Knowing, as I do, for how many years you have acted as Judge to this nation, it is with confidence that I undertake my own defense.

entries.title: Acts 24:11
segments: For you can easily ascertain that it is not more than twelve days ago that I went up to worship at Jerusalem,

entries.title: Acts 24:12
segments: Where my prosecutors never found me holding discussions with any one, or causing a crowd to collect--either in the Temple, or in the Synagogues, or about the city;

entries.title: Acts 24:13
segments: And they cannot establish the charges which they are now making against me.

entries.title: Acts 24:14
segments: This, however, I do acknowledge to you, that it is as a believer in the Cause which they call heretical, that I worship the God of my ancestors. At the same time, I believe everything that is in accordance with the Law and that is written in the prophets;

entries.title: Acts 24:15
segments: And I have a hope that rests in God--a hope which they also cherish--that there will one day be a resurrection of good and bad alike.

entries.title: Acts 24:16
segments: This being so, I strive at all times to keep my conscience clear before both God and man.

entries.title: Acts 24:17
segments: After some years' absence I had come to bring charitable gifts to my nation, and to make offerings;

entries.title: Acts 24:18
segments: And it was while engaged in this that they found me in the Temple, after completing a period of purification, but not with any crowd or disorder.

entries.title: Acts 24:19
segments: There were, however, some Jews from Roman Asia who ought to have been here before you, and to have made any charge that they may have against me--

entries.title: Acts 24:20
segments: Or else let my opponents here say what they found wrong in me when I was before the Council,

entries.title: Acts 24:21
segments: Except as to the one sentence that I shouted out as I stood among them--'It is about the resurrection of the dead that I am on my trial before you to-day'."

entries.title: Acts 24:22
segments: Felix, however, adjourned the case--though he had a fairly accurate knowledge of all that concerned the Cause--with the promise: "When Lysias, the commanding Officer, comes down, I will give my decision in your case."

entries.title: Acts 24:23
segments: So he gave orders to the Captain in charge of Paul to keep him in custody, but to relax the regulations, and not to prevent any of his personal friends from attending to his wants.

entries.title: Acts 24:24
segments: Some days later Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was herself a Jewess, and, sending for Paul, listened to what he had to say about faith in Christ Jesus.

entries.title: Acts 24:25
segments: But, while Paul was speaking at length about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgement, Felix became terrified, and interrupted him--"Go for the present, but, when I find an opportunity, I will send for you again."

entries.title: Acts 24:26
segments: He was hoping, too, for a bribe from Paul, and so he used to send for him frequently and talk with him.

entries.title: Acts 24:27
segments: But, after the lapse of two years, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus; and, wishing to gain popularity with the Jews, he left Paul a prisoner.
